question: Should generic tool-progress intent become a supported public Plugin SDK reply-payload contract for Slack and other channel plugins?
rationale: The generic seam fits the inspected Codex lifecycle and existing fast-mode metadata pattern, but adding public exports creates a lasting third-party compatibility commitment that requires owner intent.

options.title: Accept the generic SDK seam
options.body: Keep the generic progress kind and predicate, repair native-block propagation, and treat the API as a supported cross-plugin contract.

options.title: Keep progress intent internal
options.body: Replace the public exports with an internal or plugin-local seam before merge to avoid expanding the third-party API.

recommendation.title: Accept the generic SDK seam
recommendation.body: Keep the generic progress kind and predicate, repair native-block propagation, and treat the API as a supported cross-plugin contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The history connects this person to the Plugin SDK boundary, reply-payload architecture, Slack delivery, and Codex harness behavior involved in the API decision.
